title: Heuristic-seeded Kernel Arbiter for Mixed-length Streams
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our existing kernel-selection strategies either do expensive per-request probes or use coarse static heuristics that miss mixed-length traffic patterns (short chat turns interleaved with long completions). Goal: implement a low-overhead, seeded-profile arbiter that picks a small candidate kernel set per request based on architecture (GPU family + driver), quantization variant, and a lightweight sequence-length bucket computed from the prefill window and recent decode tokens.

Approach:
1) Seeded profiles: run a small microbenchmark sweep offline to produce a compact profiling table keyed by (arch-tag, quantization-tag, seqlen-bucket) -> top-3 kernels by p50/p95 cost per token and memory headroom. Store these profiles in the runtime metadata store and ship to workers at process start.
2) Per-request selection: on request arrival compute a 3-field key (arch, quant-tag, seqlen-bucket). Use the seeded profile to choose an ordered candidate list. Prefer the last-successful kernel for the same profile when available (warm-start).
3) Lightweight runtime probe policy: only probe when the request's profile has low recent confidence (few samples) or when queueing/backpressure suggests throughput-focused kernel might be preferable. Probe payloads are micro-batched probes inserted opportunistically into low-priority worker slots; probes measure tail latency and memory headroom.
4) Bandit-style exploration: run an epsilon-decay policy where epsilon scales with inverse sample count and is multiplied by a factor derived from current queue length and SLA tightness. Treat cost-per-token and latency-SLO violations as multi-objective reward signals.
5) Rollback and safety: enforce per-route latency SLO guardrails. If selected kernel causes p99 regressions or OOMs, rollback to the previous safe kernel and increase exploration in that profile.
6) Observability & telemetry: add profile_id, candidate_list, chosen_kernel, probe_result, and rollback_reason to per-request traces. Export small summary histograms per profile (p50/p95/p99, cost-per-token, sample-count, stale-flag).

Acceptance criteria: seeded profile table size < 1MB per worker; per-request selection latency added < 250 microseconds median; p95 latency for mixed-length benchmark improves by >= 8% vs baseline; no increase in OOM incidents during canary.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Microbenching offline keeps per-worker memory low and avoids expensive online full-probes for every new request, but requires periodic refreshes after driver or kernel updates.
- Opportunistic probe approach reduces probe noise at tail but may delay discovery for rare profile combinations; mitigated by warm-start and decay-based epsilon.
- Simpler seeded table faster to index than full ML-based predictor and easier to reason about in incidents.

Testing plan:
- Synthetic trace generator with mixed sequence-length distributions (chat-like short turns + long completions) to stress selection logic.
- Unit tests for profile lookup, TTL refresh, and rollback logic.
- End-to-end canary: route 5% traffic for 48h, compare p50/p95/p99, cost-per-token and OOM logs.

Rollout plan:
- Phase A: offline microbench & seeded profile ingestion (no routing changes).
- Phase B: shadow selection in production with telemetry (no effect on serving kernel).
- Phase C: 5% canary with rollback automation; expand to 25% then 100% on stable metrics.

Notes: this ticket focuses on selection/autotune logic and instrumentation only; integration with the kernel runtime glue (actual kernel swap) will be a follow-up ticket.
